title: 4D-VODS: optical data storage in glass with a self-aligning code for low-cost readers
description:
I am not a professional physicist. 4D-VODS started as a geometric intuition (storing data in the shape of engraved symbols) and grew into this conceptual study and simulator, built with the help of AI tools on standard diffraction optics. Corrections from specialists are very welcome.

Open simulator, results and documents (White Paper v1.1, Technical Note TN-001 rev. 1.1) for a concept of archival optical data storage in glass.

The study compares an 8-bit asymmetric Voxel-Wedge symbol with small amplitude/phase (APSK-16) dots under diffraction-limited optics (405 nm, NA 0.90), and introduces a Self-Aligning Micro-Matrix (SAMM) code that a low-cost bright-field microscope camera can find, orient and decode at any rotation.

All results are simulated; no physical sample has been written or read. Code: MIT License. Documents and figures: CC BY 4.0.

Version 1.1.0 changes no result: it corrects the wording of version 1.0.0 (see ERRATA.md), records the provenance of every result, checks the simulator against closed-form diffraction theory, and tests every published number automatically.
notes: Concept stage (TRL 2). Every number in the documents can be regenerated with the scripts in sim/.
